about.title: Colton Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Colton's economy runs on logistics, warehousing, and manufacturing, with much of that freight moving through corridors like I-215, I-10, and Mt Vernon Avenue. Workers in these industries face real risks: forklift accidents, falls from loading docks, and injuries from delivery trucks or contractor equipment. In California, workers' compensation is typically the only remedy against your employer, but if a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate third-party claim worth exploring. San Bernardino County crash data shows hundreds of injury collisions each year, some involving commercial vehicles tied to workplace duties. We handle workplace injury claims directly and can review your specific situation, explain your options clearly, and help you understand whether workers' comp alone covers your losses or whether more is available.

whyChoose.title: Why Injured Workers in Colton Choose Us

items.title: We Help Identify Third-Party Options
items.desc: Workers' comp usually blocks claims against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, equipment maker, or driver may still be liable. We can evaluate whether a separate claim applies to your situation.

items.title: Understanding Reporting Deadlines
items.desc: California law generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and third-party claims carry a two-year deadline. Our team can help you understand where your situation stands relative to these timelines.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: Retaliating against an employee for reporting an injury or pursuing a claim is illegal in California. If you're worried about your job status, our team can explain your rights before you take any next steps.

items.question: I was hurt at a warehouse job near I-215. Can I still get workers' comp if it was partly my fault?
items.answer: Generally yes. California workers' compensation typically doesn't require proving fault, it's meant to cover work injuries regardless of who caused them. Our team can review your specific case to confirm how this applies to you.

items.question: What if a delivery truck hit me while I was working near Mt Vernon Avenue?
items.answer: If another driver caused your injury while you were on the job, you may have both a workers' comp claim and a separate third-party claim against that driver. These are different legal paths, and our team can help sort out which applies and how they interact.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer in Colton?
items.answer: California law generally calls for reporting a workplace injury within 30 days of when it happened or was discovered. Missing this window can complicate your claim, so it's worth speaking with us as soon as possible after an injury.
